prompt:
Image 1 is the club crest. Images 2 to 5 are photographs of this athlete.

A clean product photograph of a complete Track & Field kit, laid out FLAT and neatly
arranged on a plain light grey surface, photographed from directly above.

EXACTLY ONE of each of these, in the frame, fully visible and not overlapping. A missing
item makes the plate unusable because the poses read the wardrobe from it — and a DUPLICATE
is just as bad, because two shirts leave the poses to choose which one is the kit:
- the shirt, laid flat and face up
- the shorts below it
- BOTH socks, laid out straight
- EXACTLY TWO SHOES IN THE WHOLE FRAME, never two pairs: ONE shoe seen from directly
  above, and the OTHER shoe of that same pair turned onto its side so its full profile
  and its outsole are visible. Two shoes, two views, so nothing about the footwear has
  to be guessed at when the poses are drawn from this plate.

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: A GOLD sleeveless track SINGLET exactly as photo2.png shows it: a plain ROUND SCOOP NECK with no collar and no placket, cut away at the armholes, and the body of it PLAIN GOLD all over — there is NO contrasting side panel, NO stripe and NO trim of any other colour anywhere on it, whatever the sport default says. The club badge sits CENTRED HIGH ON THE CHEST, a hand's width below the neckline: the redstone-flyers mark exactly as the crest artwork draws it — a gold winged foot inside a white field ringed by a solid dark band — about a palm across, soft-edged and moving with the fabric. It is the ONLY mark on the singlet. NO maker's logo, NO swoosh, NO sponsor, NO club name, NO player name, no lettering of any kind. The BACK of the singlet is not visible in any photograph; the DECISION is that it stays PLAIN GOLD: no number, no name, no badge and no lettering across the shoulders or anywhere else on it. This kit carries its race number on the SHORTS, and a second number across the back would print a mark this singlet does not have.
- shorts: GOLD MID-THIGH COMPRESSION SHORTS exactly as photo2.png shows them: close-fitting, plain gold all over, ending about halfway down the thigh, with a plain waistband and no stripe, no piping and no side panel. On HER LEFT THIGH, on the outside of the leg — the side that appears on the RIGHT of the frame when she faces the camera — a small WHITE RECTANGULAR RACE-NUMBER PATCH carrying the number 8 in plain black. One patch only, on her left leg only, and the number 8 appears nowhere else on the kit. NO maker's logo and no lettering on the shorts.
- socks: NO SOCKS, or none that can be seen: photo2.png and photo3.png both show BARE ANKLES above the shoe. The DECISION is that she races in no visible sock — bare skin from the hem of the compression shorts to the top of the shoe in every frame. Do not add a gold sock, and do not add a white one.
- footwear: PLAIN BLACK track shoes exactly as photo2.png and photo3.png show them after the maker's mark was taken off: an all-black low-cut shoe with black laces and a black sole, completely PLAIN and UNBRANDED — no swoosh, no stripes, no maker's mark, no logo and no lettering of any kind, on either shoe or anywhere on the sole. The same pair in every frame. This overrides the sport default of white spikes: the photographs show black, and the photographs decide what the kit looks like.
- equipment: NO IMPLEMENT IS PART OF THIS KIT. Track and field carries no ball, stick, racket or apparatus, and none appears in any photograph. What she does carry is ordinary kit-bag clutter on the way to and from the track: in photo2.png a plain dark DUFFEL BAG slung on one shoulder, and in photo3.png bags and a plain unbranded water bottle on the ground beside her — all of it unbranded, and none of it a piece of sports equipment. The DECISION for the poses is that she carries NOTHING in her hands: no baton, no bag, no bottle, no block. Starting blocks may stand on the track where a pose calls for them, but nothing is held.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest sits CENTRED HIGH ON THE CHEST of the singlet, a hand's width below the neckline, about a palm across. That position is a settled decision read off photo2.png, not a convention to be corrected: do not move it to the left chest, do not enlarge it and do not add a second mark. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.

IMAGE 2 SHOWS THIS ATHLETE WEARING THE REAL KIT. You are
photographing THOSE EXACT GARMENTS laid out flat and clean — not designing new
ones in the same colours, and not drawing what the words below describe.

WORK THROUGH THE GARMENT ELEMENT BY ELEMENT AND COPY EACH ONE EXACTLY AS THAT
PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS IT:
- the COLLAR: its shape, its colour, and whether it is laced or plain
- the SLEEVES: their length, and every band or stripe on them — HOW MANY there
  are, how wide each one is, and how far up the arm they sit
- the HEM and any waist band: its colour and its depth
- the BODY of the shirt: its colour, and any panel or piping, or none at all
- the CREST: its size, its shape, its colours and exactly where it sits
- the NUMBER: its colour, its outline, its shape, and every place it appears
- the shorts or pants, the socks and the footwear, the same way

Where the written list and that photograph disagree about how something LOOKS,
the PHOTOGRAPH IS RIGHT and the words are to be ignored. The list only decides
which items belong in the kit, which are branded, and what the photograph does
not show at all.

THE BADGE: take the artwork in image 1 and place it on the shirt UNCHANGED. Treat it as a finished graphic being applied to the garment, not as a subject to redraw or reinterpret: identical outline, identical figure inside, identical colours in identical places, identical proportions. Nothing added, nothing simplified, nothing restyled, and absolutely NO text — no club name, no letters, no word of any kind, not even small. POSITION: the badge sits CENTRED HIGH ON THE CHEST of the singlet, a hand's width below the neckline, about a palm across. That position is a settled decision read off photo2.png, not a convention to be corrected: do not move it to the left chest, do not enlarge it and do not add a second mark. Place it exactly there on the shirt as it lies facing you. SIZE: about one twelfth of the shirt's width. It is the ONLY graphic in the entire set.

Hard requirements:
- FULL-LENGTH GARMENTS ARE SHOWN AT FULL LENGTH: if the kit includes long trousers or
  pants, lay them out with BOTH legs extended completely straight, hems plainly visible
  at their full distance from the waistband — never folded under, never rolled, never
  cropped by another item, never arranged so they could be mistaken for knee-length.
  The poses copy the garment's LENGTH from this image, exactly like its colour.
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no creases beyond the fold
  of laying flat, no wear, no sweat marks. Copy what they wear, never its condition.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- Plain light grey surface, evenly lit, soft shadows only. No props, no background objects.
- BRANDING follows the list above, item by item: an item described from the athlete's own photographs keeps the manufacturer's mark it really carries, and an item that came from the sport default is plain and unbranded. Never ADD a swoosh, three stripes, a cat, a jumpman, a trefoil or a wordmark to something the list did not say has one — these marks carry no letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- No words anywhere: no club name, no player name, no sponsor, no lettering, no woven
  neck label, no care label, no watermark. The squad number appears ONLY if the kit
  description above calls for it, and no other number is invented.
NO REAL-WORLD LEAGUE OR CLUB MARKS, ANYWHERE, EVER. No NFL shield, no NBA, no MLB, no NHL,
no FIFA, no UEFA, no Premier League, no NCAA, no Olympic rings, no national federation
badge, no professional club's crest — not on a jersey, a helmet, a sleeve, a collar, a
label, a ball or a boot, not even small and not even partly hidden. The only badge that
may appear anywhere is the club crest supplied with this request. These emblems carry no
letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
